newsitem.title: USA: Ind. Gov okays workers comp benefit hike plan.
newsitem.headline: Ind. Gov okays workers comp benefit hike plan.

text.p: Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon has signed bills raising workers' compensation weekly benefits 18 percent over three years and cutting inheritance taxes, spokesman Steve Campbell said Friday.
Employer premiums are projected to increase 9 percent over four years under the plan signed by O'Bannon on Thursday.
One-time benefits for injuries that result in amputation more than double while remaining approximately 20 percent below compensation in neighboring states, O'Bannon said in a statement.
Workers who now need prosthetic devices as a result of injuries or will in the future, will receive lifetime replacement of the devices as they wear out, O'Bannon said.
O'Bannon also approved eliminating the inheritance tax for lineal descendants on the first $100,000 of an estate. The first $100,000 had been subject to $2,750 tax.
A third bill signed by O'Bannon raised weekly unemployment benefits from $217 to $252 over the next three years.
